title_en: Reporting a Rental Scam: Step by Step
summary_en: What to do in the first hour after sending money to a rental scammer — reports, banks, evidence.
body_en:
If you've just realised a room deposit or rent went to a scammer, the first hour matters more than the rest of the week. Move fast, in this order, and don't waste time feeling embarrassed — this happens to careful people too.

1. Call your bank immediately

Call your bank's fraud or hotline number straight away and ask them to try to recall or freeze the transfer. The faster you call, the better the chance the money hasn't already moved further. Every bank has a fraud hotline listed on its app or website — save it now, before you ever need it.

2. Check it's actually a scam

If you're unsure, call the ScamShield Helpline at 1799 (24 hours, or +65 6869 1799 from overseas) to check. They can also point you to your bank, but they cannot take a police report for you.

3. Make a police report

  • File a report online through the police e-services portal at police.gov.sg, or call the Police Hotline at 1800-255-0000.
  • You can also share tips or information at police.gov.sg/i-witness.
  • Bring or upload everything: chat messages, the listing, the bank transfer record, and any phone numbers used.

4. Gather your evidence properly

  • Screenshot the full chat conversation, including the listing and any promises made.
  • Save the transfer confirmation showing the amount, time, and recipient details.
  • Note down any phone number, PayNow name, or bank account used — don't delete anything, even out of frustration.
  • Write down a short timeline of what happened while it's fresh, including how you first found the listing.

5. Warn others

If the listing is still live, report it to the platform it was posted on, and consider warning the Myanmar community group you saw it in. Scammers often reuse the same listing on several people before it's taken down.

General guidance, November 2026 — not legal advice.

facts_checked.claim: The ScamShield Helpline 1799 operates 24 hours (or +65 6869 1799 from overseas) to check for scams and direct victims to their bank, but cannot take a police report
Police reports can be filed online via police e-services, by calling the Police Hotline 1800-255-0000, or tips shared at police.gov.sg/i-witness
